title: test_stop_owned_overhead_stays_within_coarse_budget flakes on CI: wall-clock ratio on shared runners fails with no code change (2 of last 15 main runs)
detail: tests/test_hook_hot_path.py asserts owned <= 1.75 x bare where both are min-of-15 wall-clock subprocess timings. On GitHub runners it went red on 79046f8 (findings-only commit; 24.7ms > 1.75 x 14.0ms) and 5c7b3c9 (43.5ms > 1.75 x 24.8ms), while the neighbouring commits with identical code were green. A machine-noise-dependent assertion that reds CI 13% of the time with no code change trains operators to ignore CI red. Fix direction: assert a deterministic proxy for the hot path (e.g. imported-module set / import count, which the hot-path perf work already constrains) as the gate, and keep the wall-clock ratio as a local-only or retried-median diagnostic, not a CI hard fail.

thread.body: Recurred on 75aab2c (v0.233.0 release push, no hook-path change): 39.2ms > 1.75 x 21.5ms. Failing ratios 1.75/1.76/1.82 — the stop hook sits AT the budget on CI runners, so noise tips it; not pure noise, a budget with no headroom on that hardware.
